title: S 47 (125th General Assembly): Voter ID
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id) not stated.
(b_no_id_remedy)
(section) Sec. 1 (7-13-710(D)(1)(a))
(quote) If an elector does not produce a valid and current photograph identification due to a religious objection to being photographed, he may complete a written statement under penalty of perjury at the polling place and affirm that the elector: (i) is the same individual who personally appeared at the polling place; (ii) cast the provisional ballot on election day; and (iii) has a religious objection to being photographed.
(section) Sec. 1 (7-13-710(D)(1)(b))
(quote) he may complete a written statement under the penalty of perjury at the polling place and affirm that the elector: (i) is the same individual who personally appeared at the polling place; (ii) cast the provisional ballot on election day; and (iii) the elector suffers from a reasonable impediment that prevents him from obtaining photograph identification.
(section) Sec. 1 (7-13-710(D)(2))
(quote) the required written statement is submitted, the county board of voter registration and elections shall find that the provisional ballot is valid unless the board has grounds to believe the written statement is false.
(c_mail_ballot_id) not stated.
(d_proof_of_citizenship) not stated.
(e_other_rule) not stated.
(other) Sec. 2: effective on approval by the Governor.
(other) version: Introduced (2022-12-01): replaces 'affidavit' with 'written statement' in 7-13-710(D)(1)-(2) (slot b); religious-objection and reasonable-impediment provisional-ballot remedies otherwise reprinted unchanged.
(other) version: Draft (2023-07-27): same operative words; strike/new marks are on the same words. No change in content found; the file is a reformatted copy.
(other) note: Same wording change as S 84 of 2021. Draft file shows the same markers once HTML styling is read (class names differ from the introduced file). No amended or enacted text saved.
(note) Off this topic: the bill sets no ID or citizenship-proof rule.
